v1.feedback: The balloon inhale/exhale cycle is a genuine morphological swerve — particles lerping to a sphere envelope then deflating back to the spiky monument is exactly the kind of transformation that earns the 'surprise' tag. Two refinements: the 19,200 particles (2400×8) may read as sparse dust rather than a taut membrane at sphere-peak — consider doubling particle density near the envelope surface during inflation (concentrate points at targetR rather than uniform radial lerp) so the balloon moment reads as skin, not fog. Second, the warm blush color shift should be more pronounced and localized — right now inflateAmount drives a global tint, but a gradient that blooms from the centroid outward (inner warm, outer still cool) would sell the 'alive inside glass' Haacke reference harder and give the eye a focal anchor during the transition.

v2.feedback: The balloon-as-inflation-of-differential-growth-membrane is a legit conceptual swerve — Hans Haacke condensation mapping to a breathing monument is sharp and the code backs it up with real mechanics (sphereDir inflation, per-particle shell scatter, sizeBoost on inflate). Two refinements: the inflate cycle should have visible asymmetry or hysteresis so it reads as organic breathing rather than a uniform scale pulse — try inflating the upper hemisphere faster or adding a slight wobble via spherical harmonics. Second, 12 particles per vert at 2400 verts is ~29k points which is fine, but the 2.4px base point size may read as dust at maxDistance=16 — consider a soft-disc sprite or slightly larger points so the membrane surface reads as a skin rather than a cloud when deflated.
